Consider $\phi = (a + bi)^3$, where $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$.
(a) In terms of $a$ and $b$, find
(i) the real part of $\phi$;
(ii) the imaginary part of $\phi$. [3]
(b) Hence, or otherwise, show that $(1 + \sqrt{3}i)^3 = -8$. [2]
The roots of the equation $z^3 = -8$ are $u$, $v$ and $w$, where $u = 1 + \sqrt{3}i$ and $v \in \mathbb{R}$.
(c) Write down $v$ and $w$, giving your answers in Cartesian form. [2]
On an Argand diagram, $u$, $v$ and $w$ are represented by the points U, V and W respectively.
(d) Find the area of the triangle UVW. [3]
Each of the points U, V and W is rotated counter-clockwise (anticlockwise) about 0 through an angle of $\frac{\pi}{4}$ to form three new points U′, V′ and W′. These points represent the complex numbers $u'$, $v'$ and $w'$ respectively.
(e) Find $u'$, $v'$ and $w'$, giving your answers in the form $re^{i\theta}$, where $-\pi < \theta \le \pi$. [4]
(f) Given that $u'$, $v'$ and $w'$ are the solutions of $z^3 = c + di$, where $c, d \in \mathbb{R}$, find the value of $c$ and the value of $d$. [3]
It is given that $u$, $v$, $w$, $u'$, $v'$ and $w'$ are all solutions of $z^n = \alpha$ for some $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$, where $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
(g) Find the smallest positive value of $n$. [3]
